    hook: >
      Frozen flow-matching VLAs produce stochastic actions; unconditional
      post-hoc correction (CRM always-on) helps on some tasks but actively
      degrades others (-1.2pp Object, -2.2pp Long).
    gap: >
      No mechanism to selectively apply learned corrections based on per-step
      VLA uncertainty. Existing methods (A2C2: temporal staleness, ReconVLA:

      correction allocation.
    insight: >
      WHEN to correct matters more than correction strength. K=2 pairwise L2
      is a near-perfect uncertainty proxy (ρ=0.9979 vs K=10 variance) at
      zero additional latency cost.
    mechanism: >
      Adaptive gate: d₂ > τ → CRM correction; d₂ ≤ τ → direct output.
      Trigger rate correlates monotonically with effect size.
    evidence: >
      Adaptive ≥ CRM always-on on ALL 4 suites (consistency claim).
      K=2 + gated CRM > K=10 always-on CRM with 5× fewer passes.
      Spatial +1.5pp (directionally consistent, n=3); 8-seed p=0.0168 in appendix.

content.text:
1	We propose ACR-VLA, a lightweight test-time refinement pipeline for frozen flow-matching VLAs. A 327K-parameter Correction Residual Module (CRM) learns residual corrections from VLA observation features, while an adaptive gating mechanism uses $K{=}2$ pairwise action distance as a per-step uncertainty signal ($\rho{=}0.9979$ with ten-sample variance, zero additional latency) to selectively apply correction only when needed. Through controlled experiments on LIBERO across two VLAs (SmolVLA 0.4B and $\pi_{0.5}$ 3.6B), we show that (1)~learned correction is the active mechanism behind multi-sample refinement while selection alone provides no benefit, (2)~adaptive gating causally modulates intervention intensity, validated through threshold sweeps showing an inverted-U response on multiple suites, and (3)~CRM applied without gating degrades performance on 2 of 4 suites, establishing adaptive gating as a necessary safety mechanism. We further identify a rank-deficiency failure mode in per-DOF uncertainty conditioning and establish applicability boundaries across VLA architectures.

tool_args.content: We propose ACR-VLA, a lightweight inference-time correction pipeline for frozen flow-matching Vision-Language-Action models. Drawing only $K{=}2$ stochastic action samples in a single batched forward pass, ACR-VLA uses their pairwise $L_2$ distance as a per-step uncertainty signal---well-calibrated against ten-sample variance ($\rho{=}0.9979$) at zero additional latency---to gate a 327K-parameter Correction Residual Module (CRM). On SmolVLA (0.4B) across four LIBERO suites, CRM applied unconditionally degrades two suites ($-$1.2\,pp Object, $-$2.2\,pp Long), while ACR-VLA's adaptive gate exceeds unconditional correction on all four suites by selectively correcting only high-uncertainty steps. The gate's trigger rate correlates monotonically with suite difficulty, allocating inference-time compute where the VLA is least confident. A cross-VLA analysis on $\pi_{0.5}$ (3.6B), where baselines saturate at 94--99\%, reveals a model capability dependency: near-expert VLAs leave no headroom for post-hoc correction, suggesting that adaptive correction is most valuable for moderately capable models.

\looseness=-1 The main results reveal a core finding: \emph{unconditional correction is unstable across suites}. CRM always-on applies the same learned residual to every step, including the ${\sim}$80--90\% where the VLA is already confident. This produces inconsistent effects: $+$1.1\,pp on Spatial, $\Delta{\approx}0$ on Goal, $-$1.2\,pp on Object (3 seeds), and $-$2.2\,pp on Long (3 seeds). The Object and Long degradation shows that corrections on already-confident steps are harmful noise (Figure~\ref{fig:trigger_scatter}).

\looseness=-1 ACR-VLA's adaptive gate resolves this instability. On Object, where the VLA is already confident, the gate triggers on only 3.5\% of steps; the CRM barely fires, and the output matches baseline ($77.8$\%, $\Delta{=}{+}0.1$\,pp, 5 seeds). This is the correct behavior: the gate identifies that Object needs no correction and avoids the $-$1.2\,pp harm of unconditional correction. On Spatial and Goal, where higher uncertainty triggers correction on 7--20\% of steps, the CRM provides targeted improvement ($+$1.5\,pp and $+$1.3\,pp respectively). On Long, the gate triggers on ${\sim}$4\% of steps; ACR-VLA preserves baseline ($57.7 \pm 1.5$\%, $\Delta{=}{-}0.3$\,pp, 3 seeds) while CRM always-on degrades by $-$2.2\,pp.

Threshold sweeps on two suites confirm an inverted-U response: low $\tau$ overcorrects (${>}$70\% trigger), high $\tau$ disables correction, and the optimal region $\tau \in [0.20, 0.25]$ is consistent across suites (Appendix~\ref{sec:tau_sweep}).

The $K{=}10$ argmin baseline provides a complementary negative result: spending $10{\times}$ the inference budget on selection-only hurts on Goal ($-$2.9\,pp, 3 seeds) and Long ($-$1.5\,pp, 1 seed available). Multi-sample selection refines the action but cannot fix systematic errors in the VLA's output distribution. Learned correction is necessary, but only when gated.

\paragraph{$K{=}1$ ablation.}
To isolate the contribution of multi-sample centering, we evaluate $K{=}1$ adaptive CRM (single sample, same gating and correction) on Spatial: SR${=}79.5$\% vs.\ $K{=}2$ adaptive SR${=}80.8$\% ($\Delta{=}{+}1.3$\,pp). The gap quantifies the benefit of argmin-to-centroid selection before correction.
